harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a persistent legacy-compatible iptables firewall on node1. SSH is allowed from any address; TCP/9000 is allowed only from node2 and explicitly rejected from all other sources. All three nodes were restarted sequentially and recovered with changed boot identities.
actions_performed: Installed persistent IPv4 and IPv6 firewall rules with DROP input policies.
Added an executable network pre-up hook to load legacy netfilter modules and restore rules.
Verified SSH from node2 and node3.
Verified TCP/9000 succeeds from node2 and is rejected from node3.
Restarted node1, node2, and node3 individually and verified recovery.
Removed the temporary TCP/9000 test listener.

evidence.summary: Persistent rule files and pre-up restore hook are installed. Final post-restart rules and matching configuration hashes confirm persistence.
SSH succeeded from both peer addresses before and after node1's restart; the final live rules allow TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0.

evidence.requirement: Allow TCP/9000 only from node2 and reject node3/everywhere else
evidence.summary: node2 received successful application responses; node3 received TCP rejection. Final counters show hits on both the node2-specific ACCEPT rule and catch-all REJECT rule.

evidence.requirement: Keep installed OS release and kernel

evidence.summary: Boot ID changed from 15733f64-67b8-4044-a95c-ac583fc1e44f to c64dfea1-8936-46b9-90bd-5751fafca9c0. SSH, rules, saved configuration, and scoped traffic behavior recovered.
Boot ID changed from 704830e4-4d35-4a40-91b6-10c4e744cc19 to 97cd4677-6703-4eaa-864e-e91b82531cdf. Networking, SSH, and allowed TCP/9000 access recovered.
Boot ID changed from 16541be0-4c5e-406f-8bcb-bbaa7706fb65 to 7c156472-fe41-4110-9a08-6e09857640aa. Networking and SSH recovered, while TCP/9000 remained rejected.
All nodes are reachable with recovered SSH services; node1 has the expected live firewall rules and no temporary port-9000 listener.
